paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates minADE\_20 performance (with a left-pointing arrow in the label) as a function of the number of in-context examples, comparing two selection methods. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 0 to 8 with ticks shown at regular intervals (0, 2, 4, 6, 8). The y-axis is labeled “minADE\_20 (←),” uses a linear scale, and ranges approximately from about 0.126 to 0.14 (tick labels are shown around the 0.13–0.14 region). Two solid lines with circular markers are shown: the ST-ES series is a blue solid line with blue circle markers, starting near 0.139 at 0 examples, dropping to about 0.129 at 1 example and to roughly 0.127 at 2 examples, reaching a low point around 0.126–0.127 near 4 examples, then rising to about 0.129–0.130 around 6–7 examples and ending near 0.129–0.130 at 8 examples. The Random series is an orange solid line with orange circle markers, starting near 0.14 at 0 examples, dropping to about 0.132 at 1 example, staying around roughly 0.132–0.133 at 2–3 examples, increasing to about 0.134 at 4 examples and about 0.136 at 5 examples, dipping to around 0.131 at 6 examples, then increasing again to about 0.136–0.137 at 7 examples and ending near 0.138–0.139 at 8 examples.
